open_points.subject: FlowEdge endpoint identity
open_points.text: a flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node (A05 rule 2), never the `flow_id`
open_points.question: Is the empty string forbidden as a FlowNode `node_id`, so it identifies only a flow-boundary endpoint?
options: Reserve the empty string exclusively for flow-boundary endpoints and refuse a node with that `node_id`
Allow an empty FlowNode `node_id` and distinguish it from the boundary by other context
open_points.default_guess: Reserve the empty string exclusively for flow-boundary endpoints and refuse it as a FlowNode `node_id`.

open_points.subject: FlowEdge guard skipping with constants
open_points.text: A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node, is not executed and is recorded `skipped_by_guard`
open_points.question: How does this rule apply to an input port supplied by a FlowConstant, which has no incoming FlowEdge: does the constant count as an available delivery, or does the empty set of incoming edges make the port satisfy “every incoming edge” and skip the node?
options: A delivered FlowConstant makes the input available and prevents this skip condition
The rule examines only FlowEdges, so a constant-only input is skipped
Constants count as incoming sources for this availability test
open_points.default_guess: Treat a delivered FlowConstant as an available input and do not skip a node merely because that port has no incoming FlowEdge.

open_points.subject: FlowEdge skip propagation and NodeExecution status
open_points.text: or coming from a skipped node
open_points.question: Which upstream NodeExecution statuses make a source a “skipped node”: only `skipped_by_guard`, or also `upstream_failed`; and consequently should a downstream node whose input comes from an `upstream_failed` node be recorded `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`?
options: Only `skipped_by_guard` sources propagate `skipped_by_guard`; failure-blocked paths remain `upstream_failed`
Both non-executed statuses count as skipped and propagate `skipped_by_guard`
Both count as unavailable, but each propagates its own status
open_points.default_guess: Only `skipped_by_guard` propagates `skipped_by_guard`; inability caused by a failed upstream path remains `upstream_failed`.

open_points.subject: FlowConstant and StoredValue creation
open_points.text: `value`: the `value_id` of a StoredValue (M21) of `value` carriage — a constant is never a file — written when the version is composed, whose class the composing agent declares with the constant
open_points.question: Does the compose action receive literal content, schema and class and have the kernel mint or reuse its StoredValue and `value_id`, or does it receive an already-existing `value_id`; if the latter, what does “written when the version is composed” mean?
options: The agent supplies literal content, schema and class; the kernel derives the `value_id` and writes or reuses the StoredValue during composition
The agent supplies an existing `value_id`; composition only references that StoredValue
The action permits either an inline literal or an existing `value_id`
open_points.default_guess: The agent supplies literal content, schema and class, and the kernel derives and stores or reuses the StoredValue during composition.
